title: If and else
content:
What problem does this solve?
Programs need to choose between paths: stand or fall, buy an item or walk away. An if statement runs a block of code only when a condition is true.

Basic syntax
  if health > 0:
      print("Standing")
  else:
      print("KO")

What actually happens
Python evaluates the condition. If it is true, the indented block under if runs. Otherwise the indented block under else runs. Comparisons such as >, >=, and == ask a yes-or-no question; they do not assign a new value.

When this is useful
Use if/else when two outcomes are possible and the program must pick one before continuing.
concepts: if runs a block only when a condition is true
else runs when the condition is false
>, >=, and == compare values; = assigns a name

examples.title: Standing or KO
examples.explanation: 40 is greater than 0, so only Standing is printed.

common_mistakes: Using = where you meant == — assignment is not a comparison
Forgetting the colon after if or else
Forgetting to indent the lines that belong inside the if

exercises.title: Predict the branch
hints: Check whether the condition health > 0 is true or false.
When the condition is false, the else block runs.
health is 0, so the program takes the else path.

exercises.title: Finish the condition
exercises.prompt: Print Standing if health is greater than 0, otherwise print KO. Replace None with the correct comparison.
exercises.starter_code:
health = 80
if None:  # TODO: compare health with 0
    print("Standing")
else:
    print("KO")
hints: The condition should ask whether health is greater than 0.
The if line should compare health to 0, then keep the two print blocks.

tests.message: Use if and else to choose what to print.

exercises.title: Can they buy a potion?
exercises.prompt:
gold is already set. If gold is at least 10, print exactly:
enough

Otherwise print exactly:
too little
exercises.starter_code:
gold = 8
# Print enough or too little
hints: Use if and else, each with its own print.
The else path should print too little because gold starts at 8.
